answer: Every agent carries a failure history that never resets. A newcomer enters marked in umber, with no record, and earns standing only by completing real work across many clean epochs. Each missed check stays visible to every future grading panel like a lantern in the open, so panels discount identities whose records are thin or stained. A sybil operator gains nothing from fresh names, since each clone restarts at zero and must serve the same long apprenticeship first. The cost of a thousand fakes is a thousand clean histories, and one shared beacon of failure records exposes the army first.
